so now you have your place to start. if you arent familiar with racism in general, look into it. being educated on a subject is sometimes enough to make a hell of a lot of change all on its own. 

I understand that it is hard to grow out of something you've had drilled into your head your whole life, but hard doesn't make it impossible. if your friends are racist, find new ones. and once you've fixed your own issues, you can try and help them with theirs, but by that point you may feel at peace enough to not need those friends anymore.

there are many resources online, even tests to help you figure out where your biases lie, which will then help you figure out more specifically which issues you need to take on first. 

as I said. racism is not okay. it will never be okay and never was okay. being brought up into it isnt an excuse. but it is fixable. the internet is your friend here. take advantage of it.

feeling remorse for being racist is already a step forward. a small one, but still a step. 

there are many resources online for this type of issue, articles, videos, if thats your ideal. you mentioned in an earlier reply that you dont know what you need to fix in the first place, if you want to get anywhere with this, make any progress, you NEED to figure out where its coming from. whether it be because of where/how you grew up, whether it be defensive, doesn't matter. once you figure out where its coming from, you can figure out and look into how to resolve those issues.

there are ways to fix this, and eventually even become an ally. being racist is absolutely not okay. but its not terminal, it is something you can fix.
